transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, AE on the account. We also have Diego, our SE, and Priya from solutions. How's everyone?
[00:06] Nina (Solstice): Hi Maya, thanks. I'm Nina. We have Ethan, Samir and Olivia on. Doing well.
[00:10] Diego (Redwood SE): Great, quick agenda: demo of hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints, show Console Optimize suggestions, then security Qs. We'll leave 10–12 minutes for next steps.
[00:20] Ethan (Solstice): Sounds good. Quick bit of context: we run a clinician-facing search across a corpus of annotated notes, ~2M docs, Elastic today. Latency matters — under 200ms median on search — but relevance is the blocker.
[00:33] Maya (Redwood): Good, that matches what you shared in the form. Nina, success criteria you mentioned in the intake — can you restate?
[00:38] Nina (Solstice): Sure. Better precision on top-3 results for diagnostic queries, keep p95 latency close to current (within 1.5x), and reasonable cost per query. Also compliance: SOC2, KMS, and audit logs.
[00:50] Priya (Redwood): We'll show how hosted API handles those and options for dedicated/private later.
[00:56] Diego (Redwood SE): Jumping in — first demo is embeddings. We're using the hosted embeddings endpoint, you can batch requests. Note that embeddings units are charged per vector, and we have a per-request throughput model. In the Console you'll see ingestion job hints.
[01:12] [screen share starts] Diego: Here is a quick notebook — POST to /v1/embeddings with your texts, we recommend batching 64–256 depending on seq length. For clinical notes we often choose 64 to keep memory predictable.
[01:27] Ethan: When you say batching, what's the tradeoff? Latency vs cost right?
[01:30] Diego: Exactly — bigger batches improve GPU utilization and lower unit cost but increase tail latency. Our Optimize/Console suggests a batching window that balances p50/p95 for your 1k qps like traffic.
[01:42] Nina: Do you do any on-the-fly quantization for embeddings?
[01:45] Diego: The hosted pipeline returns float embeddings; we provide quantized model variants you can pick in the model catalog if you want smaller vectors and lower costs. But for clinical semantics we usually stick to full precision unless you need the cost win. Also, be aware of small numeric differences across quantized variants.
[02:00] [timestamp jump] Maya: Now reranking — typical flow is retrieve candidates via Elastic (ANN), then call Redwood's rerank endpoint with top N candidates and the query for a final sort.
[02:12] Samir (Solstice): Do you expect us to send raw docs or doc IDs?
[02:15] Diego: Send doc IDs and the candidate payload; we fetch the stored embeddings if you choose to manage them in Redwood, or you can pass embeddings inline. For speed we recommend sending precomputed embeddings if you have them in your pipeline.
[02:30] Ethan: In our case we compute embeddings at ingest into Elastic. How would that work with Redwood?
[02:34] Diego: Two options: 1) Keep embeddings in your store and call rerank with inline embeddings; 2) push embeddings to Redwood vector storage via the ingestion API and point rerank to those IDs. Option 2 gives us more caching and lower per-query latency for rerank because we can avoid transfer overhead.
[02:50] Nina: Can you explain the caching — you mentioned KV cash in the notes earlier?
[02:55] Priya: Ha, KV cache — yes sorry, sometimes transcript tools make it KV cash. It's KV cache (key-value) for autoregressive models; for rerank we use candidate-level caching and prefix cache when doing multi-turn reweights.
[03:09] Diego: For rerank, our system caches dense vectors and rerank model hidden states where applicable so repeated queries are faster. We also support a candidate cache keyed by document ID+query signature.
[03:24] Ethan: Latency numbers — what should we expect for top10 rerank calls?
[03:28] Diego: On hosted, typical p50 is ~30–60ms for a small rerank model (128–256 hidden), p95 might be ~150–250ms depending on sequence lengths and batch settings. If you need sub-100ms p95 we recommend Dedicated pools or moving more embedding storage into Redwood to avoid network hops.
[03:48] Nina: That's close to our constraint but p95 250ms might be pushing it. Cost-wise how does hosted compare to self-managed?
[03:56] Maya: Hosted gives a pay-as-you-go cost per embedding + rerank call. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-query unit cost as you commit. There's also Redwood Optimize which suggests batching/caching to reduce unit costs. We'll send a pricing rundown.
[04:12] Olivia (Solstice, Security): On compliance — do you support BYOK/KMS? How are audit logs exposed?
[04:18] Priya: Yes, for Private we support customer KMS integrations, and for Hosted we offer customer key encryption at rest with managed KMS options. Audit logs are available in Console with export to S3 or SIEM. We also have SOC2 type II.
[04:32] Olivia: Do you have a network diagram for hosted vs private? We need to show our InfoSec team.
[04:36] Maya: We'll include the network diagram in the security pack; I'll add Olivia as a recipient.
[04:40] [screen changes — Console] Diego: Console view — here's a rerank tuning lab. You can upload a relevance set (pairs: query + ground truth doc), run evals and see precision@k, MRR. You can tweak the re-ranker temperature, candidate count N, and reweighting features.
[04:58] Ethan: Could you show an example where you rerank a clinical query?
[05:01] Diego: Sure — example query: "post-op fever differential" — we pulled 10 candidates from Elastic. Sending those candidates to rerank with the query, here's ranking before and after. You can see precision@3 moves from 0.42 to 0.68 after rerank.
[05:20] Nina: Those are promising numbers, is that on our data?
[05:23] Diego: That was a synthetic demo using a small anonymized sample you provided earlier. In the sandbox we'll run the same eval against your 5–10 sample queries you provide.
[05:33] Samir: About hallucinations — are there safety controls? We can't have the model invent treatment plans.
[05:38] Priya: Rerank models are discriminative and score candidates; they don't generate free-form text in the rerank flow. For generation we do have guardrails and can restrict tool-calls, but in your use case rerank reduces hallucination risk because it's selecting from vetted docs.
[05:52] Ethan: For the sandbox, can we run a side-by-side bench with our Elastic-only pipeline?
[05:56] Diego: Yes, we can run a micro-benchmark comparing Elastic topK vs Elastic + Redwood rerank. We'll measure p50/p95 latency and precision metrics. We'll instrument token counts and cost for hosted calls.
[06:10] Nina: About data residency — our corpus must remain in the US region only. Is hosted region restriction possible?
[06:16] Maya: Yes, we host in multiple regions. For Hosted API you can pick region and we can pin to US-east or GovCloud for more restricted customers; we'll include the region options in the security pack.
[06:28] Olivia: Retention — can you purge uploaded embeddings or set TTL?
[06:32] Priya: Yes — data retention policies and purge APIs exist. For Private deployments you manage retention entirely. For Hosted you can set auto-delete windows or execute a purge with an audit trail.
[06:45] Ethan: One more question on throughput: we might burst during morning rounds — can hosted handle burst?
[06:50] Diego: Hosted supports burst up to a degree; for sustained high QPS Dedicated pools are recommended. We also support autoscaling policies on Dedicated; hosted has rate limits and can be tuned with commit tiers.
[07:03] Maya: Quick bit about cost saving levers from Optimize: prefix caching for repeated queries, smaller rerank model for cheaper calls, and suggestion to offload heavy embedding ingest to a background job.
[07:16] Nina: For our evaluation, what would you recommend as a minimal pilot?
[07:19] Diego: 1-week sandbox with 2k anonymized notes, 20 sample queries, and an eval harness. We'll run batch embeddings ingest, run rerank evals, and provide a metric dashboard in Console.
[07:32] Samir: Sounds reasonable. Any pointer on anonymization expectations?
[07:35] Priya: Remove direct identifiers, and for extra caution you can hash PHI fields. We can sign an NDA if needed; but for the sandbox anonymized data is fine.
[07:44] Olivia: On the legal side — will you accept our DPA?
[07:47] Maya: We have a standard DPA; legal can review and we can work any clauses around data residency. I'll loop in sales-legal after this call.
[07:58] [screen ends] Maya: Recap — we'll send pricing and security pack, Diego will create sandbox and run bench, Solstice sends sample queries and anonymized notes, timeline target start next week.
[08:10] Ethan: One more nit — when you say "rerank model" can we bring our own model?
[08:14] Diego: At present the hosted rerank endpoint runs Redwood-managed models but we support custom model uploads for Private deployments and Dedicated if you want full control. For the sandbox you can request a tuned variant from us.
[08:28] Nina: Competitive question — how do you compare to Pinecone + a hosted scoring service?
[08:32] Priya: Pinecone is vector store; Redwood bundles vector serving + rerank model + operational tooling and Console. The edge is integrated caching, reweights and Optimize recommendations. Also fewer moving parts for you to glue.
[08:46] Olivia: For audit logs — are they tamper-proof and how long retained?
[08:50] Maya: Logs support immutability options and we can set retention in the Console; we'll provide export examples to your SIEM.
[08:59] [end of main content, closing minutes — notes and small crosstalk]
[09:05] Maya: Any last questions?
[09:07] Ethan: No, thanks — excited to try the sandbox.
[09:10] Nina: Thanks team.
[09:12] Maya: Great, we'll follow up with the docs and invite.
[09:15] [meeting ends — automatic transcript cutoff]
